name: Scabiosa
family: Caprifoliaceae, the honeysuckle family (the scabious group, once its own family, Dipsacaceae, the teasel family)
grown_as: A pincushion flower. William's library lists Scabiosa incisa 'Kudo Pink': a compact perennial about 30 cm high and wide with bright pink pincushion flowers from spring to late autumn. Described as that, not as the taller annual sweet scabious (Scabiosa atropurpurea). ⚠️ CHECK the leaf shape against William's plant.
habit: A compact, mounded clump 25 to 35 cm high and as wide, with leaves mostly near the base and many slender, nearly bare flower stems above.

leaf.arrangement: Basal leaves in a loose rosette; stem leaves in opposite pairs
leaf.type: Simple but deeply cut (pinnately) into narrow lobes
leaf.outline: Oblong to lance-shaped overall, 5 to 12 cm; stem leaves smaller and more finely cut
leaf.margin: Each lobe with a few teeth
leaf.stalk: Basal leaves stalked; stem leaves stalkless

flower.form: A pincushion: a domed head of many small florets with a frilly ring of larger florets round the edge
flower.petals: Each floret's petals are joined into a small tube with five lobes. The outer florets are much larger and lopsided, their outward-facing lobes enlarged and frilled, so together they make a ring of 'petals'
flower.centre: A dome of small, closed inner florets studded with long pale stamens like pins in a cushion
flower.behind: A ring of narrow, pointed, hairy green bracts under the head, shorter than the outer florets
flower.carried: Alone on long, slender, wiry, bare stalks well above the leaves, facing up

fruit: A round, straw-coloured ball like a drumstick head. Each seed sits in a papery, ribbed, funnel-shaped collar with a star of five dark bristles at its centre, so the ball looks spiky and starry.
seedling: Two small oval smooth seed leaves on short stalks. The first true leaves are oval and toothed; later leaves become lobed.
winter: Semi-evergreen: a low clump of grey-green basal leaves stays at the soil.

leaf: basal leaf deeply cut into narrow toothed lobes
stem leaves in opposite pairs, smaller and finer
bloom: domed pincushion of tiny florets studded with pale stamens
outer ring of larger frilly florets, lopsided outwards
seed: small seed with a papery funnel collar
a star of five dark bristles at the top, like a shuttlecock
young: low clump of grey-green cut leaves
flower: many slender bare stems each topped by one pink pincushion
seedhead: round straw-coloured balls of seeds with bristly stars
dormant: low clump of grey-green leaves at the soil

look_alikes: Small scabious (Scabiosa columbaria) is the wild chalk-grassland plant, lilac with finer leaves. Sweet scabious (Scabiosa atropurpurea) is a taller annual, often deep maroon. Field scabious (Knautia arvensis) has four-lobed florets, bristly stems and seeds without a funnel collar. Devil's-bit scabious has undivided leaves and all florets the same size.
